title: Large personal ST/DOS source-port and format-recovery discovery
summary: Personally screen 690 candidate URLs and add 10 projects, with twelve explicit non-promotion decisions.
notes: Root assistant personally searched 16 GitHub query routes across Amiga, Atari ST, CPC and DOS, screened 690 unique URLs and inspected 23 available repository trees. Ten additions and twelve explicit non-promotions; already-tracked GODS toolkit left unchanged. Two additional retrieval leads, m602_recon and mapedit-decomp, could not be inspected and are not classified as recovered sources. Distinguish native source ports, game-script VMs, hardware services, instruction-level recompilation, bootstrap byte repacking and substantive historical ASM. No upstream game, compiler, installer, patcher, emulator or hardware program executed.

sources.reason: Native C99/SDL3 map editor derived from the MAPEDIT executable recovery; inspected connected-region numbering and original-layout records.
Native TypeScript game logic ported from Paul Stevens CSBWin, itself recovered from Atari ST binary. Inspected typed monster-attack logic and source-line mappings.
Source-derived port of Kent Dahls 1996 DOS game with original Pascal/archive and extracted assets; inspected combat functions mapping to original source lines.
Maintained two-unit C/assembly source for all three episodes, original-toolchain packed equality claimed upstream. Inspected GAME1.C and actual host generation design.
Maintained exact TASM oracle plus native C player/game/service translations and SDL3 host. Inspected player-state contracts and original dispatch quirks.
Early reconstruction research identifies EXEPACK root, ten MZ overlays and 16 resource containers. Inspected symbolic put-string probe and actual outer-container format study.
Maintained exact ASM and structured C routines over canonical original memory; inspected decimal renderer and separate completeness ledger.
Tkinter/Pillow editor decodes and rewrites encrypted maps and EGA tile banks for three episodes. Inspected structured row parsing and background/foreground ownership.
Source-built patcher and recovered compression/font/text/VM literal formats enable Czech translation. Inspected bounded relative-jump relocation code and exact input validation.
Native C++ game modules from DOS decompilation, with structured combat/save field registration. EGA/CGA/Hercules support does not imply running original x86 code.
Contemporary Pico/Mega robot firmware and companion software; search collision, not a requested retro-platform game/application recovery.
Actual source platform is Z80 MSX-DOS, not IBM PC DOS. Useful MSX recovery but outside this focused platform pass.
Modern native test-runner infrastructure, not a reconstructed historical game/application. Keep tooling separately scoped.
Original 68000 code runs under game-specific Amiga runtime/library/chip emulation. Not a native high-level game-source recovery despite port label.
Instruction-level static recompilation with 68000 interpreter fallback and emulated Amiga hardware. Preserve architecture audit rather than classify as recovered high-level engine.
Runs original 68000 code against an emulated Amiga environment; native reimplementation remains a plan. Do not equate executable compatibility with source reconstruction.
Bootstrap currently splits and rejoins original EXE parts; matching C is planned. Byte-identical concatenation is not recovered game source.
Primary recovered executable is Windows MDKD3D.EXE, not DOS MDK. Retain for a Windows-source pass; original data compatibility alone does not change source provenance.
Targets 1997 Windows Hercules with PSX references, not DOS. Source recovery is real but outside the requested source-platform focus.
Public tree contains README and packaged executable tool archive, not reviewable converter/engine source; planned map editor is not released source.
README and binary distribution claims do not expose converter source or reproducible format implementation. Retain lead without promoting source recovery.
Graphics conversion and patched Lion King executable described, but no public textual implementation in inspected tree. Binary-only tools/patches are not a new source reconstruction.
